title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction: Context: E443 treats the transverse vibrations of an elastic lamina AF clamped in a wall at A and free at F (a cantilever). In modern form this is the Euler–Bernoulli equation K c^2 y'''' + (mass) y_tt = 0. Euler separates variables, y = cos(θ²t)·X(x), with X = A cos(θx/b) + B sin(θx/b) + C e^{θx/b} + D e^{-θx/b}. The clamped–free conditions give the frequency equation in Φ = θa/b; the previous page calibrates the stiffness constant cc by one static deflection experiment. This page does two things. (1) It summarizes the mode structure. The 1st 'species' (mode) never crosses the axis AB and only touches it at A. The 2nd crosses once, the 3rd twice, the 4th three times, and so on: mode n has n−1 interior nodes, 'as was shown long ago'. Euler adds that this solution is 'maxime particularis': it covers only certain curve shapes and is 'still very far' from a general solution such as had been obtained for strings (the d'Alembert/Euler arbitrary-function solution). (2) It begins computing the reactions the wall must supply to hold the lamina. Take a point Y. The elementary (inertial) forces p dx acting on the part YF can be viewed two ways. Their sum is ∫p dx, i.e. the shear force. Their moment about Y is ∫dx∫p dx, i.e. the bending moment. The moment equals −Kcc (d²y/dx²) (the bending-moment/curvature law). Since the shear is the x-derivative of the moment, ∫p dx = −Kcc (d³y/dx³). Euler recalls the abbreviation b^4 = 2bkcc; this is consistent with cc = Ik^3/(3Ki) and b^4 = (2/3)Ibk^4/(Ki) from p.465. The next page evaluates both quantities at x = a (the clamp) using the explicit A, B, C, D. This gives the shear force and moment the wall exerts on the embedded piece Aa, as functions of time ∝ cos θ²t.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The shear = derivative of moment step and the sign convention (forces treated as pulling downward) are consistent.

The neighbouring page p.465 states the overtone frequencies grow like squares of natural numbers. For a clamped–free beam they grow asymptotically like squares of odd numbers, (2n−1)², which is only proportional to n² in a loose sense. This is not on this page. The p.465 transcription also shows an inconsistent stray K in the expression for α, which may be a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Mode n of the cantilever has n−1 interior nodes (crossings of the axis).
ideas.modern_name: Oscillation (node-count) property of eigenfunctions of a fourth-order Sturm–Liouville-type problem.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Observed by D. Bernoulli and Euler (1742–44). The general theory is due to Sturm (1836) for second order, and to Kellogg and Gantmacher–Krein (oscillation kernels, 1930s–50) for beams.
ideas.where_published: E65 Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I De curvis elasticis; also Euler's other lamina papers (E40-era and 1770s).

ideas.what: Recognition that the separated-variable (modal) solution is particular, and that a general solution like the one for strings is lacking.
ideas.modern_name: Completeness of eigenfunction expansions / modal superposition for the beam equation.
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Bernoulli's superposition principle (1753). Rigorous treatment by Fourier, Poisson and Cauchy (19th century); completeness via Sturm–Liouville and Hilbert-space theory.
ideas.where_published: Discussed in Truesdell, The Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788 (Opera omnia II 11/2).

ideas.what: Shear force = ∫p dx = −Kcc y''' and bending moment = ∫dx∫p dx = −Kcc y'', used to compute dynamic root reactions at a clamped end.
ideas.modern_name: Shear force/bending moment relations (V = −EI y''', M = −EI y''); dynamic support reactions of a vibrating cantilever.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moment–curvature law: Jakob Bernoulli and Euler. Shear relation in beam theory: Euler; systematized later by Navier and others.
ideas.where_published: Euler's elastica and lamina papers; analysed by Truesdell (1960).

deep.surprise_reason: All content is known: node counting of cantilever modes, the acknowledged lack of a general solution, and the computation of shear and moment at the clamp. Truesdell's history of rational elasticity covers E443 in detail. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'atque a ſolutione generali' – the print has 'à' (accented a).
Otherwise the transcription matches the image. The equation b⁴ = 2bkcc is correctly read, as are ∫p dx = −Kcc(d³y/dx³) and the moment = −Kcc(ddy/dx²).
